What Paw-to-Paw keeps about you

This is the record of what the app keeps and who can see it. It is short because the app is small. Every line here is kept by a specific piece of the app, and JK checks the list each time the app changes.

What we keep

We keep your name, your mobile number, your block (never your unit), your dogs' names, and your answers to the sign-up questions.

Your dog's breed, birthday and licence tick if you gave them, and the vaccination date JK has seen in person — only JK can write that date.

The days, times and short notes you post when you need a hand. A note can't be changed once it's posted, so say anything new in the group.

Who offered, and who was picked.

When your dog was handed over and handed back. Those times are taken by Paw-to-Paw, not your phone, and once logged nobody can change them, JK included.

What a host needs to know about your dog, if you write it: food, routine meds, a vet limit, and when to call you. The version the host was shown is kept with that swap.

A photo at each handover, if one is taken. Photos are kept with the handover record. When a household leaves, its photos go on a list JK can see and deletes by hand.

Each time your household opens the app: just that it happened, not what you looked at, and not when you say it happened.

If you sign up from outside Tengah, we keep your answers and tell you if a pack opens near you. We don't count you as a neighbour, and you can leave the same way anyone can.

The mobile number you type when you sign up is kept as you typed it. It only becomes your household's number once JK has checked it with you in person, when you meet. Paw-to-Paw never sends a code or a text message to it.

If JK gives you a code to get back in — a new phone, a lost one — it works once, for thirty minutes. Paw-to-Paw never keeps the code, only a scrambled version that is thrown away when it is used or runs out, and JK's record that he gave you one holds no code. Until you choose your new PIN nothing else in the app opens, and nobody but JK can start any of this.

Who sees what

Your household's details are seen by you and by JK. Nobody else can read your row.

Once you have met another household, each of you can see the other's name, block and the line about when you can usually host — never the unit, and never the mobile number.

When you post that you need a hand, every approved household can see it — your name, your block, your dog's name, the day and hours, and any note — unless your dog's booklet date isn't current, in which case only you and JK can.

When you offer to help, the household that posted sees your name, your block, when you offered, and your hosting line — never why you could or couldn't. Other offerers see no list and no count.

Once a hand is sorted, everyone in the pack can see which household has the dog that day. Once your dog is handed back, it leaves everyone's feed.

The household that takes your dog sees your dog's card at the door. The card is kept with that swap exactly as it was that morning, so a change you make later applies next time.

Photos taken at a handover are seen by the two households on that swap and by JK, nobody else. Once the handover is logged nobody can change or remove them, JK included.

JK can see how often each household opens the app. Nobody else can.

The app never passes your number to anyone. Messages go through JK or the pack's WhatsApp group.

Until JK has met you, the number you typed is seen only by you and JK, and only you can change it.

The short code on your waiting screen, and JK's note that he has checked your number with you, are seen only by you and JK. Only JK can write the note, and it is cleared if you change your number. The code is not a password and it signs nobody in.

Points

Your household has a points balance — one point for each hand you host, one for each you use, starting at two. Only your household and JK can see it.

Points aren't money. Nothing in the app can buy, sell or move them; they are counted from swaps that happened.

There is no public board today.

Leaving

You can leave the pack yourself, from the app, without asking anyone — the button is under My household, and on the waiting screen.

Leaving wipes your name, number, block, answers and your dogs' details, and deletes the record of when you opened the app. Nothing can be typed back in afterwards, and your sign-in shows only that you left. Open requests are cancelled; nobody leaves while a dog is out.

A swap is the other household's record as much as yours, so who met whom and who minded whom stays on the record for good.

Your swaps stay on the record without your name — the times, the card the host was shown and any note you posted — so nobody's points change because you left. Your pack number is never given to anyone else.

Who has the keys

Two people can reach the keys: the project account and one second seat, both named in the accounts file. No company, no one else.

Your data is stored in Singapore.

We don't read your location. The camera is used for one photo at a handover, and only if you allow it; the photo library is not touched.

No ads, no analytics companies, no tracking.

What JK promises

These are kept by JK, not by the app's code. They are written down here so you can hold him to them.

If Paw-to-Paw stops, everything is deleted and you will be told first.

If a public board ever exists, it will show how many times you've helped, never your balance.

Ask JK and he will tell you exactly what is left about you.

When you leave, JK deletes the photos of your dog from storage within a week.

Last checked 1 Oct 2026. Questions: message JK, or ask in the pack's WhatsApp group.
